billTitle: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran that have not been authorized by Congress

speakers.name: Tammy Duckworth
speakers.quote: Congress has never authorized war with Iran. What we are seeing is an unconstitutional conflict — one that has cost lives and that the American people never consented to. This resolution is about restoring the constitutional order.
speakers.summary: Duckworth argued the Iran military operations are unconstitutional without explicit congressional authorization, invoking her own combat veteran experience to emphasize the cost in American lives.

speakers.name: Lisa Murkowski
speakers.quote: I have long believed that Congress cannot outsource its war-making power to the executive branch. The Constitution is clear. I will vote yes on this discharge motion today.
speakers.summary: Murkowski crossed party lines to support the resolution, citing the constitutional obligation of Congress to authorize military force, a position she has held consistently across administrations.

speakers.name: Tom Cotton
speakers.quote: Removing our forces now — mid-operation — would hand a strategic victory to the Ayatollahs and signal to every adversary that America's resolve can be broken by political maneuvering in the Senate.
speakers.summary: Cotton argued that withdrawing forces mid-conflict would embolden Iran and undermine ongoing operations, characterizing the resolution as a dangerous signal of weakness to adversaries.
